short: Scalogram CNNs (M06) and ImageNet weights (M03) were new for imagined speech but standard: effects not isolated; 93% imagination sits on a 43.77% pre-stimulus floor (Table 1).
position: The paper changes the decoder (M06) to scalogram CNNs and training (M03) to ImageNet initialisation [@dash2020decoding]. Neither appears among the 16 earlier imagined-speech decoders of any electrophysiological signal (Appendix), yet both are standard: the CNN-versus-ANN gain changes representation and classifier together, as the authors concede, the sensor mosaic does not beat per-sensor scalograms for imagination, and no network is trained from scratch. Evaluation (M12) follows the usual within-subject trial split; the authors report that the pre-stimulus window is classified above chance by all methods (43.77% for AlexNet SST-CNN, 20% theoretical chance) and attribute it to carryover. The floor is equal across methods, so it does not explain the CNN gain, but the 93.24% for imagination comes from a window that follows reading of visibly different phrases and does not separate imagery from reading carryover and preparation.
